  Readable gloss: "A diminutive of ὄψον (cooked food, relish), designating a small or prepared fish typically eaten as a side accompaniment to bread. All five occurrences appear in John's Gospel in two feeding contexts. In the feeding of the five thousand, a boy provides five barley loaves and two ὀψάρια (John 6:9, 11). In the post-resurrection lakeside breakfast, Jesus has fish already laid on charcoal (John 21:9), asks the disciples to bring some of their catch (21:10), and serves bread and fish (21:13). The Spanish 'pescaditos' beautifully preserves the diminutive quality, as does French 'petit poisson.'"

Distinguished from ἰχθύς (fish as a living creature), ὀψάριον emphasizes the culinary dimension.     Existing Spanish translations: pescaditos, pescado, pescados
